text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Enforcement officers from the Commercial Vehicles Licensing Board were given a taste of what members of the public had endured all this while when they went "undercover" to check on complaints against errant taxi drivers.
- Applications to local universities for the 1998 intake can be made at the touch of a button using the telephone or through the Internet, Education Minister Najib Razak said.
- A scout was killed and 15 others injured when lightning struck their camp on Gunung Ledang during a heavy downpour yesterday evening.

- Putting the August 3 blackout firmly behind it, Tenaga Nasional Bhd has set alight ambitions to invest abroad next year under the second phase of executive chairman Ahmad Tajuddin Ali's plans for the utility company.

- The four counters that have been the talk of the market since they were suspended last month -- DCB Holdings Bhd, Rashid Hussain Bhd, Maybank Bhd and Kwong Yik Bank Bhd -- were requoted yesterday at prices that are within expectations.
- Promet Bhd, in a bid to become a world-class infrastructure, maritime engineering and construction group, is now looking at acquiring a construction company to add to its stable.
- The Cabinet wants employers to reward loyal and dedicated workers to encourage them to be more productive, Human Resources Minister Lim Ah Lek said.
